text: Now let's move on to the next step and go through every step of creating your first invoice.
First, we fill in our company details. They then follow along on every invoice, so you don't have to enter them each time.
Here you can also add your logo, address, phone number, organisation number and the other details.
Save – and the first step is done.
Next, we add a client. You can choose between a private person and a business – here we take a business.
To create a client, the company name is enough – but in general, everything you fill in, like the organisation number and contact person, appears neatly on the invoice.
The client's details are saved in the system and always stay available. The address, email and phone number you enter here are also included in the invoice.
Here you choose the payment terms, the currency and other details that are linked to every invoice we send to this client.
In this step, you create articles that you'll later use when invoicing. An article contains the VAT rate and the unit.
For example materials, or services for private persons or businesses. Since this is construction work for a company, we choose zero percent VAT.
Here we choose the client we created earlier and the project. Your reference and the order reference are filled in automatically.
We choose the article – and the project name ends up in the description.
Then we set, for example, a price of 595 and a quantity of 50 hours.
Tap Create invoice – and your first invoice is ready. This is how it will look once all your company details and the client's details are filled in.
